title: Bind every guarded alt/opt fragment to acceptances, and back

facts.note: Source subject kind is 'interlocking'. An observer must classify an artifact as an interlocking; no evidence that this classification is observable today.
Validation runs at CONFIRM and is confirm-blocking. It covers every interlocking at CONFIRM, including unchanged ones. A phase observer is needed.

values: interlocking contains a guarded alt/opt fragment or a flow-branch acceptance
facts.note: Needs a parser that finds guarded fragments and flow-branch acceptances in the interlocking, whether or not they changed.

values: guarded alt/opt fragment added or edited
facts.note: Optional discovery signal for firing early during authoring. It is NOT a required gate: the rule also applies to unchanged artifacts at CONFIRM.
Optional discovery signal only. It is never a required gate.

fires: At CONFIRM, an interlocking contains guarded alt/opt fragments or flow-branch acceptances, including ones that were not changed in this plan
Planner adds a guarded alt or opt fragment to an interlocking and must list its acceptance(s)
Planner writes a flow-branch acceptance and must reference back the guard/fragment it covers
An interlocking edit removes a guarded fragment's only bound acceptance
doesNotFire: Interlockings with no guarded alt/opt fragments and no flow-branch acceptances (linear flow only)
Acceptances for the main linear flow that are not flow-branch acceptances

given: An interlocking contains guarded alt/opt fragments or flow-branch acceptances (changed or not)
when: The planner authors or edits the interlocking, or the plan reaches CONFIRM
then: Bind both ways: every guarded alt/opt fragment references at least one acceptance, and every flow-branch acceptance references back the guard/fragment it covers.
prefer: Give fragments and guards stable ids and list acceptance refs on each fragment
On each flow-branch acceptance, cite the guard_id/fragment_id it covers
avoid: Guarded alt/opt fragments with no acceptance
Flow-branch acceptances bound to no guard or fragment
One-way binding: refs on fragments without back-references, or the reverse
Binding a fragment to an unrelated or placeholder acceptance just to pass the check
why: Bidirectional binding keeps branches traceable. Each guarded fragment points to its acceptances, and each branch acceptance points to the fragment it covers.
evidence: Every guarded alt/opt fragment has at least one acceptance_ref that resolves to an existing acceptance
Every flow-branch acceptance has a guard_id/fragment_id back-reference that resolves to an existing guard/fragment
verifier_detail: Validation family: coverage; template: source_has_required_target; variant: planner_train_interlocking_fragment_acceptance_binding
Failure evidence fields: interlocking_id, fragment_id, guard_id, acceptance_ref, missing_side
Term fragment_binding: every guarded alt/opt fragment binds to acceptances and flow-branch acceptances bind back to guards/fragments

additions.text: Use stable ids on fragments and guards, and cite acceptance refs and back-references
additions.justification: Concrete moves taken from the failure evidence fields (fragment_id, guard_id, acceptance_ref). They add no new obligation.

additions.text: Binding to a placeholder or unrelated acceptance to pass the check
additions.justification: The authoring brief requires a metric-gaming anti-pattern. It follows from the binding's intent.
The source has no 'why'. This sentence only restates the traceability that the statement implies and claims nothing about test execution.

additions.text: References must resolve to existing acceptances/guards/fragments
additions.justification: A binding only counts if its reference resolves. The rule imposes no locality restriction.

additions.text: No split proposed. Both directions form one bidirectional binding check, verified by a single validator that reports missing_side.
additions.justification: The two directions are the same decision and are verified together.
